itens.titulo: Should You Buy Bank of America Stock After a $1.2 Billion Regulatory Fine?
itens.descricao: Should You Buy Bank of America Stock After a $1.2 Billion Regulatory Fine? Yahoo Finance
trechos: Following its third-quarter earnings report, Bank of America's (NYSE: BAC) stock fell 4.7% on Oct.
14 in its worst performance in 18 months.
At one point, the stock fell almost 9%, a huge move for a stock like Bank of America.
Not only did the bank report weak results, it also disclosed a $1.2 billion regulatory fine for money-laundering violations.
In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia.
For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia.
Continue » A disappointing quarter Bank of America reported $0.91 per share in profit on revenue of $30.12 billion.
Both numbers came up short of Wall Street's expectations, but excluding the $1.2 billion fine, the bank would have reported $1.08 in earnings per share, missing estimates by only $0.02.

itens.titulo: Bitcoin Volatility Hits 2.5-Year Low as Traders Brace for 30% Move
itens.descricao: Bitcoin Volatility Hits 2.5-Year Low as Traders Brace for 30% Move Yahoo Finance
trechos: But an unusually tight trading pattern is raising fears of a sudden price swing, with $80,000 emerging as the level that could decide its direction.
BTC trades near $82,538, up 0.92% in 24 hours.
According to Barchart, the bands are now just $5,368 apart, equivalent to roughly 6.5% of Bitcoin's price.
Bitcoin's Last Two Volatility Squeezes Ended in 30% Swings The warning comes from Bitcoin's own price history.
In May, a similar squeeze near $82,000 ended with Bitcoin crashing almost 30% below $58,000.
Three months later, another squeeze near $63,000 produced the opposite result.
Bitcoin surged more than 35% toward $87,000.
Despite last week's technology-stock selloff and oil prices above $100, Bitcoin closed the week above $82,000.

itens.titulo: Nvidia’s Valuation and Narrative Risk are High Now So Act Accordingly
itens.descricao: Nvidia’s Valuation and Narrative Risk are High Now So Act Accordingly Yahoo Finance
trechos: Quick Read - NVDA posts six straight earnings beats with revenue up 106% to $96B, yet the stock has barely moved over the past month.
- NVIDIA invested nearly $50B in frontier AI labs and expects those balance-sheet-supported customers to drive roughly a quarter of next year's business.
- Wall Street's consensus target of $329 implies 54% upside, but a beta of 2.2 leaves the stock highly exposed to any sentiment reversal.
NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) trades at $214.13.
Data Center revenue reached $89.02B last quarter, up 117%, and the company is worth about $5.17 trillion.
Shares fell 6.61% over the past week while the S&P 500 slid 1.97%.
Revenue Doubling at 25x Forward Earnings Looks Cheap Revenue of $96.22B rose 105.8%, and EPS of $2.22 beat the $2.09 consensus, a sixth straight beat.
Guidance calls for $108.0B next quarter, and management expects "to grow revenue by approximately 70% in fiscal 2028.
